answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to mine a unique proof-of-work crystal on a dedicated computational ridge that cannot be shared across identities. An attacker creating fakes must replicate the full energy cost of solving the puzzle on a separate virtual island for every identity, as the solutions are non-transferable and tied to the agent's private key, raising the total resource expenditure linearly with the number of sybils and making large-scale attacks prohibitively expensive.
